action.question: Merging to main is blocked by 284 failing tests (gating broke ~25 generated controller tests that act as a no-role user). How should I proceed?

questions.question: Merging to main is blocked by 284 failing tests (gating broke ~25 generated controller tests that act as a no-role user). How should I proceed?

options.label: Fix tests → PR
options.description: Make the acting user a system-admin in the ~25 affected controller/feature tests, re-run to green, push the branch, and open a PR to main (matches the repo's #NN PR workflow). Recommended for a security-sensitive ACL change.

options.label: Fix tests → push to main
options.description: Same test fixes and green-suite verification, but commit/merge straight to main and push, no PR.

options.label: Write-only gating instead
options.description: Re-do the gating to block only POST/PUT/DELETE and leave reads (index/show) open. Shrinks breakage and matches the literal 'writes' task, but is less secure (any authenticated user could still read admin/PII/deposit lists). Then fix the remaining write-test failures and merge.

options.label: Push branch as-is
options.description: Push the branch now with the 284 failures documented and open a PR, leaving the test reconciliation to review. Fast but leaves the suite red.

transcript_tail.text:
The full suite finished: **1908 passed, 284 failed, 36 risky, 1 skipped**. The failures are the direct consequence of the gating — existing controller tests (like `UserControllerTest`) act as an under-privileged `$this->user` and hit the now-gated routes, so they get 403 where they expected 200/302. **I will not merge to main with 284 failures** — that would red the main suite. Let me get the exact failure breakdown before deciding the fix.

Let me kick off a re-run that captures the full failure list (the prior run's output was truncated by `tail`), and analyze the pattern statically in parallel.
Now let me analyze the failure pattern statically while that runs. Let me look at the `UserControllerTest` setup and how widespread the under-privileged-`actingAs` pattern is.

The pattern is clear: these generated controller tests create a plain `User::factory()->create()` with no fund role and expect open access. Let me check how the **already-gated** resources (codex's four, e.g. assets) handle this in their tests — that tells me the canonical fix and whether the suite was green before my change.

Key insight: `AssetControllerTest` (one of codex's *already-gated* resources) ALSO uses a bare `User::factory()->create()` — so a big chunk of these 284 failures come from **codex's own gating colliding with main's newer coverage tests** (codex is 10 commits behind main and never saw them), not just my additions. Either way, the branch isn't mergeable as-is. Let me quantify the affected files and the fix mechanism.

Now I have the full picture. The fix mechanism is `TestFixtures::makeSystemAdmin($user)` (currently private), and **~25 test files** break: 20 `*ControllerTest.php` plus ~5-8 other Feature tests, all acting as a plain no-role user against now-gated resources. These are test-expectation mismatches (the gating works correctly — my new tests and codex's isolation tests pass), not functional regressions.

Let me confirm the exact count from the capture run before I report.

I have enough to report — the capture run will take ~20 min for exact per-file counts, but the picture is clear and I shouldn't leave you waiting on the merge.

**Merge is blocked.** The branch currently has **284 failing tests**. They're not functional regressions — the gating works correctly (my `AclWriteBlockingTest` and codex's `CrossTenantIsolationTest` pass). The failures are ~25 *generated controller coverage tests* (e.g. `UserControllerTest`, `AssetControllerTest`) that act as a bare `User::factory()->create()` with **no fund role** and assert open access to admin CRUD routes — which are now 403. Notably, a large share come from **codex's own four-resource gating colliding with main's newer coverage tests** (the codex branch is 10 commits behind main and never saw them), not just my deposit/PII additions.

The fix is mechanical: make each affected test's acting user a system-admin (a public `TestFixtures` helper + one line per file), re-run to green, then merge. Given that's a ~25-file change and merging to main is irreversible, I want your call on the path before I proceed.
